security.footnote: Agentry checks a credential; it does not sign anyone in. Terminate TLS in a reverse proxy in front of it, so a token never crosses the network in the clear.
security.saveFailed: Could not save the security settings

readOnly.title: Read-only mode
readOnly.intro: Turn it on to show the panel to someone without letting them change anything: every request that would write is refused with 405.
readOnly.label: Refuse every write
readOnly.note: Answering a permission prompt still works, so a chat someone is watching can be unblocked, and so does this switch. Everything else, including the token below, is refused until it is turned off.

access.title: Access
access.intro: Choose what a request must carry to be answered. Only the health check stays open.

none.label: None
none.body: Anyone who can reach the port can use Agentry. Fine on a loopback-only local install; not on a network.

token.label: Token
token.body: Every request must carry the bearer token set below. This browser keeps it in its own storage.

oidc.label: OIDC
oidc.body: Every request must carry a JWT signed by your identity provider, for the issuer and audience given here.

access.issuerHint: The provider's URL. Its signing keys are fetched from there.
access.audienceHint: The audience a token must be issued for.
access.clientIdHint: Optional. The client your proxy signs users in with.
access.oidcNoLogin: Agentry only validates a JWT: it never talks to a token endpoint. The credential comes from a proxy in front of it, or is pasted on the sign-in screen.

missing.token: Set a token below before turning token authentication on: without one nobody could get in.
missing.oidc: The issuer and the audience are required.

token.title: Require a token?
token.body: From the next request on, everything is refused without the token. This browser already holds it, so you stay signed in; anything else that uses the API needs the token too.
token.noStoredToken: From the next request on, everything is refused without the token, and this browser does not hold it: you will be asked for it on the sign-in screen. Keep the token you set at hand.

oidc.title: Require an OIDC token?
oidc.body: From the next request on, everything is refused without a JWT from your identity provider, and this browser will ask for one on the sign-in screen. Make sure you can get one before you continue.

token.title: Token
token.intro: Agentry keeps only a hash of the token, so it can be shown once and never again. Rotating replaces it: the old one stops working at once.
token.recovery: Lost the token and locked out? Restart the server with {{token}} set to a new value and {{reset}}=1. That value replaces the stored token once, and the change is written to the audit log; a restart with the variables still set changes nothing.
token.removeBlocked: Switch the mode away from Token before removing it.
token.shownOnceBody: It is shown only this once. If you lose it, rotate the token. This browser already uses it.
token.ownHint: At least {{min}} characters. It is not shown again.

rotateConfirm.title: Rotate the token?
rotateConfirm.body: The current token stops working at once, for everyone who holds it. This browser switches to the new one.

removeConfirm.title: Remove the token?
removeConfirm.body: Its hash is deleted. Turning token authentication on again needs a new one.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: Every request that changed something, newest first: who, what, and how it ended. The request body is never recorded, since it holds prompts and secrets.
audit.noneHint: A write to the API will appear here.
audit.statusInvalid: The status is a code such as 404 or a class such as 4xx.
audit.noMatchHint: Drop a filter, or try a shorter part of the path.

cli.title: Claude Code
cli.notPinned: not pinned (the image installs whatever was current when it was built)
cli.upToDate: Claude Code is up to date.
cli.updateHow: Agentry does not update the CLI inside a running container, so a restart always gives the same version. Rebuild the image with CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION={{latest}} (Docker Compose: set it in .env and run docker compose build), or pull a newer Agentry image. On a plain install, run claude update.
cli.note: Checked when you ask and once a day, never when a page loads. It reads the npm registry, not claude.ai.

tokenSource.credentialsFile: credentials file from an interactive login
tokenSource.cswap: claude-swap: it owns the credential file and rotates between accounts

account.savedDetail: It applies to every new run. Verify it with a real request.
account.cswapNote: claude-swap manages several accounts, so the wrapper injects no token of its own — a credential set here would override the active account. Switch accounts from <anchor>Accounts</anchor>.
account.loggedInNote: “Logged in” only means a credential is configured; the CLI does not validate it. Use the verification to be sure.
account.secretHint: Stored in the wrapper data volume and applied to every new run. It overrides credentials from the container environment and is never returned by the API.

settingsGuided.hooksIntro: Hooks run shell commands at lifecycle events; the event payload arrives as JSON on stdin. Keep scripts in <mono>hooks/</mono> and edit them in the <anchor>Files tab</anchor>.

hookEvents.PreToolUse: Before a tool runs. Matcher: tool name pattern, e.g. Bash or Edit|Write. Can block the call.
hookEvents.PostToolUse: After a tool succeeds. Matcher: tool name pattern.
hookEvents.UserPromptSubmit: When the user sends a prompt, before Claude sees it.
hookEvents.Notification: When Claude Code sends a notification.
hookEvents.Stop: When the main agent finishes responding.
hookEvents.PreCompact: Before compaction. Matcher: manual or auto.
hookEvents.SessionStart: When a session starts. Matcher: startup, resume, clear or compact.

settingsGuided.statusLineHint: statusLine: command whose output is shown as the status line.
settingsGuided.defaultModeHint: permissions.defaultMode: how tool calls are handled when no rule matches.
settingsGuided.ruleSyntax: Rule syntax: <mono>Tool</mono> or <mono>Tool(specifier)</mono>, e.g. <mono>Bash(git status)</mono>, <mono>Bash(npm run test:*)</mono>, <mono>Read(./secrets/**)</mono>, <mono>WebFetch(domain:example.com)</mono>, <mono>mcp__server__tool</mono>. Deny wins over ask, ask wins over allow.
settingsGuided.additionalDirsHint: permissions.additionalDirectories: extra directories Claude may work in.
settingsGuided.envHint: Applied to every session. Values are masked here but stored in plain text in the file.

orchestration.workflowTitle: Every task a subagent of one Claude Code session
orchestration.graphHint: Every task runs as its own Claude Code process and can get its own worktree and branch, merged into one at the end. The choice for tasks that change code.
orchestration.workflowHint: Every task runs as a subagent of one Claude Code session, through a workflow script generated from these tasks: cheaper, and a resume replays what had finished from Claude Code's cache. All of them work in the project directory, with no worktrees: for tasks that read, analyse or review.
orchestration.synthesize: Run a final agent that synthesizes all task results
orchestration.worktree: Give each task its own git worktree and branch
orchestration.askPermissions: Ask me when a worker needs permission
orchestration.askPermissionsHint: Prompts appear on the worker's run page for you to allow or deny. Without this a worker has nobody to ask, so anything not listed below is denied automatically.
orchestration.toolsHint: A worker has nobody to ask, so the CLI denies anything not pre-authorised here. Leave empty to rely on the permission mode alone.
orchestration.worktreeHint: Workers then never write over each other, and never edit the checkout Agentry is running from — an orchestration that edits this repo restarts the wrapper and kills itself. Needs the directory to be a git repository.
orchestration.noTasksHint: Add tasks and wire their dependencies.
orchestration.title: Orchestration
orchestration.subtitle: Split an objective into tasks and run them as parallel agents with dependencies
